context: Accessible force-directed network graph with 150 nodes across 6 communities, paired with a synced sortable/filterable data table below — a data visualization with strong accessibility engineering focus
first_impression: Clean and light with deliberate color choices, but the network topology is nearly invisible at rest — the connections that make a network graph meaningful barely register against the background
what_works: Paul Tol bright palette is a genuine accessibility-conscious design choice rather than schemeCategory10 defaults; the keyboard instruction bar with styled kbd elements and the canvas+table layout pairing show thoughtful structural design
what_doesnt: Edges rendered at 18% opacity in the default (no-selection) state are effectively invisible — the core data encoding of a network graph (its connections) cannot be read without hovering or selecting, undermining the visualization's purpose; many nodes scatter to the canvas boundary, particularly bottom and left edges, giving the layout an uncontained feel
